MBBS in Australia for international students is available through direct-entry medical programmes and graduate-entry Doctor of Medicine courses. A few universities still use the MBBS title, while many award an MD, BMed/MD or BMedSc/MD. The title matters less than accreditation, entry route, total cost and the pathway to medical practice.

The short answer is this. School leavers may enter selected five or six-year medical programmes after Year 12 or an equivalent qualification. Students who already hold a bachelor’s degree usually consider a four-year graduate-entry MD. Both routes can lead towards provisional registration and supervised postgraduate training when the programme is accredited by the Australian Medical Council.

Before choosing a university, answer three questions. Does the programme accept your qualification? Can your family fund the complete route rather than only the first deposit? What professional step follows graduation?

Students comparing the wider destination can first review how Australian study works for overseas applicants. Medical universities add admission tests, interviews and clinical compliance to that process.

Fees and entry rules change. Australian universities review their requirements independently, so use the official course page and formal offer as the final authority. Check the structure of MBBS in Australia programmes individually before making academic decisions.

Is MBBS Available in Australia, or Is It Called an MD?

MBBS in Australia still exists. James Cook University offers a six-year Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery. Most other well-known medical schools now use qualifications such as Doctor of Medicine, Bachelor of Medical Studies/Doctor of Medicine or Bachelor of Medical Science/Doctor of Medicine.

In Australia, an MD can be the primary professional medical qualification. It does not always mean that the applicant was already a doctor before entering the course. UNSW Sydney, for example, accepts eligible school leavers into a combined BMed/MD programme. The University of Queensland offers a four-year MD for graduate applicants and approved pathway students.

Parents often continue to say MBBS when an offer letter says MD. What matters is whether the programme is accredited, accepts overseas applicants and leads towards the correct professional pathway.

Students can compare the practical differences between MBBS and MD qualifications, but they should choose by route and outcome rather than by familiar letters.

Direct Entry After Year 12 or Graduate Entry?

The right route depends on your current academic position.

Graduate-entry MD

Completing the final year of a bachelor’s degree

Check both prior-study restrictions and future graduate-entry eligibility

Direct-entry medicine commonly assesses school results, science prerequisites, an aptitude test and an interview. For MBBS in Australia after Year 12, Monash University uses ISAT and a Multiple Mini Interview for international selection. UNSW considers academic performance, an accepted aptitude test and an interview. James Cook University uses academic results, a written application and an interview process.

Graduate-entry medicine usually requires a bachelor’s degree, a competitive GPA, an approved graduate admission test and an interview. UWA, Flinders University, the University of Sydney and the University of Melbourne use graduate-entry selection, although their formulas and minimum standards differ.

Here is the counterintuitive part. A four-year MD is not necessarily the shortest route. A school leaver may first need three or four years to complete a bachelor’s degree, taking the total pathway to seven or eight years. An eligible five-year direct-entry programme may be faster.

Applicants with time away from education should also check how Australian institutions assess a study gap. Do this before paying for an admission test.

Do not rank universities by brand alone. Australian universities differ in route, selection method and overseas seat availability. Remove courses that do not accept your qualification, then compare cost, admission probability, location and clinical placements. Use this comparison of Australian medical schools after that first filter.

Eligibility and Entry Requirements

There is no single national entry formula for MBBS in Australia. Australian universities set their own academic, subject, test, English and interview standards.

Direct-entry applicants may need Chemistry, Mathematics or Biology, plus a highly competitive school result. UNSW currently states an academic rank equivalent to ATAR 96 or above for direct international applicants, together with an accepted aptitude test and an interview. Monash lists Chemistry, ISAT and an MMI for international direct entry.

Graduate-entry applicants normally need a recognised bachelor’s degree and GPA. UWA allows international MD applicants to submit GAMSAT or MCAT, with final ranking based on the admission test, GPA and interview. Flinders also accepts an approved graduate admission test from eligible international applicants.

NEET is not a universal Australian university admission requirement. Indian applicants who may return home should separately confirm the latest National Medical Commission rules.

UNSW Medicine MD Direct Entry TOEFL Requirements for International Students

UNSW currently lists TOEFL iBT 94 overall for the Bachelor of Medical Studies/Doctor of Medicine, with at least 25 in writing and 23 in reading, listening and speaking. The same official table lists IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with at least 6.0 in each component and PTE Academic 65 overall with at least 54 in each component.

English evidence is only one part of selection. Applicants must also satisfy the academic, approved test and interview requirements. Students deciding between English tests can compare PTE and TOEFL formats, then use the official medicine requirement to make the final choice.

MBBS Fees in Australia for International Students

MBBS fees in Australia for international students vary by university, route and fee year. For MBBS in Australia, universities publish indicative amounts that may rise during the course. The total cost also changes with programme length and city.

Based on official figures reviewed for this article, annual tuition ranges from AUD 71,383 at JCU in 2026 to AUD 109,328 for UQ’s four-year MD in 2027. UNSW lists AUD 95,500 for the first year in 2026 and an indicative AUD 647,000 to complete its six-year programme.

Tuition is only part of the budget.

Cost item

Planning approach

Tuition

Use the international annual fee and estimate possible annual increases

Living costs

Allow roughly AUD 30,000 to AUD 45,000 a year, depending on city and lifestyle

Health cover

Consider the cost of required health insurance arrangements for the study period

Tests

Include admission-test and English-test charges where relevant

Clinical costs

Budget for checks, vaccinations, equipment, uniforms and placement travel

Relocation

Include flights, rental bond, temporary accommodation and initial setup

At UNSW, published first-year tuition is AUD 95,500. Adding an illustrative AUD 35,000 living budget takes the year above AUD 130,000 before health cover, flights and setup costs. This planning example shows why the first payment is only one part of the overall education budget.

Students should compare living costs across Australian cities and understand what international student health cover normally includes before committing to a programme.

Low Cost MBBS in Australia

Australia is not a low-cost medical-study destination. JCU has the lowest published annual tuition among the verified examples in this guide, but a six-year course can still create a large total bill. A four-year programme with a higher annual fee may be cheaper for a student who already holds the required bachelor’s degree.

The useful calculation is total pathway cost, not the lowest fee in one column.

MBBS in Australia for Pakistani Students Fee Structure

Pakistani applicants normally pay the same published international tuition as other overseas students in the same programme. The current examples in this guide range from about AUD 71,383 to AUD 109,328 per year, before living costs, Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) and other academic or clinical expenses. The same principle applies to Bangladeshi, Indian, Nepali and other international applicants.

How to Apply to Study MBBS in Australia

Medicine applications often begin 12 to 18 months before the course starts.

  1. Identify whether you fit direct entry or graduate entry.
  2. Confirm that the programme accepts international students and holds AMC accreditation.
  3. Check academic prerequisites, prior-study restrictions and English scores.
  4. Register for the required admission test before its deadline.
  5. Prepare transcripts, passport, grading information and course-specific forms.
  6. Apply through the university or the required admissions centre.
  7. Prepare for the MMI or structured interview.

For 2027 entry, applicants should not rely on a 2026 deadline list. JCU’s international medicine application for 2027, for example, required documents by 30 June 2026. UNSW states that 2027 applications are open and interviews for international applicants run from June into the following January. Always check official university sources for the latest requirements and deadlines before submitting an application or paying any related fees.

Australia Study Costs and OSHC

Most international medical students pursuing MBBS in Australia need to consider tuition fees, living costs, and essential study-related requirements. Study Australia provides official information on planning study costs and other requirements for international students.

Applicants also need a Confirmation of Enrolment, Genuine Student information, financial evidence where required, and suitable health insurance. Study Australia’s OSHC guidance states that international students must hold Overseas Student Health Cover for the duration of their studies in Australia.

PG in Australia After MBBS: Internship and Medical Licensing

PG in Australia after MBBS can describe two different pathways.

Graduates of an accredited Australian medical programme usually apply for provisional registration and complete PGY1 training. The Medical Board of Australia requires at least 47 weeks of full-time-equivalent supervised training, including a minimum of four terms in different areas of clinical care. After satisfactory completion, a graduate may become eligible to apply for general registration.

Doctors who completed their primary medical qualification outside Australia follow an international medical graduate pathway. Depending on the route, this may involve the Australian Medical Council, Ahpra, English standards, examinations and supervised practice.

An Australian medical degree does not guarantee an internship, employment opportunity, permanent residency outcome, or specialist-training position. Students should understand post-study pathways and available opportunities based on their individual circumstances and official guidance.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can international students study MBBS in Australia after Year 12?

Yes. Eligible school leavers can apply to selected direct-entry or combined medical programmes. They may need strong school results, science prerequisites, an approved admission test and an interview.

What is the duration of MBBS in Australia?

Direct-entry medicine usually takes five or six years. A graduate-entry MD normally takes four years after a bachelor’s degree.

What are MBBS in Australia fees per year?

The official examples reviewed range from AUD 71,383 to AUD 109,328 per year. The actual amount depends on the university, programme, fee year and study load.

Is NEET required for MBBS in Australia?

Australian universities do not use NEET as a universal admission requirement or rank applicants by a NEET score. Indian students should still check current NMC rules if they plan to practise in India later.

What should I know about GAMSAT 2026?

Applicants using GAMSAT 2026 for a later intake must confirm the university’s score-validity period and application deadline. A valid score does not guarantee an interview or offer.

Can I receive a full medical scholarship?

Possibly, but full scholarships are rare and highly competitive. Many awards are partial or exclude medicine.

Is an internship guaranteed after graduation?

No. Internship allocation depends on accredited positions, state policies and graduate categories. Ask the university for current international-graduate information before accepting an offer.

Final Decision

For MBBS in Australia for international students, the correct order is route, eligibility, total cost, accreditation and professional planning. University reputation comes after those checks.

Choose a compact shortlist of programmes that genuinely fit your qualification and finances. Then verify every fee, test and deadline through the linked official source. Students who need help matching their academic profile, budget and preferred route can request a personalised assessment before paying application or test fees.
